claims.text: The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is in an as-cast or homogenized state.
Warm rolling at 800–1000°C will refine the grains of HfZrTiTa0.53.
A short post-rolling anneal will relieve internal stresses while preserving fine grains.
The treatment will produce a fine-grained microstructure with increased grain-boundary density.
The additional grain boundaries will act as barriers to crack propagation.
The additional grain boundaries will promote dislocation activity.
The proposed crack-propagation and dislocation mechanisms will enhance tensile ductility and uniform elongation.
Fine grains will maintain high yield strength through Hall–Petch strengthening.
Grain refinement will not substantially alter the alloy's impact-triggered energetic response.
Excessive annealing or high-temperature exposure may coarsen the grains and reduce the treatment's benefits.
The reported baseline yield strength of HfZrTiTa0.53 is 786 MPa.
The reported baseline compressive strength of HfZrTiTa0.53 is 1314 MPa.
The reported baseline terminal strain of HfZrTiTa0.53 is 13.5%.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported baseline energetic impact response.
At room temperature and tensile strain rates of 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1, uniform elongation will increase by at least 50% relative to the stated 13.5% baseline.
The treated alloy's yield strength will remain within 10% of 786 MPa.
The treated alloy's compressive strength will remain comparable to the 1314 MPa baseline.
The treated alloy's impact-triggered energy release will remain comparable to baseline.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% reported value is labeled only as terminal strain and ambiguously as tensile/compressive in the baseline, but the prediction treats it as a tensile uniform-elongation baseline. Terminal strain, compressive terminal strain, and tensile uniform elongation are not interchangeable metrics.

Impact-triggered energy release is to be tested at 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1 or at 'similar' rates, which are quasi-static to moderate rates rather than conventional impact strain rates; thus the stated test conditions do not clearly test the claimed impact-triggered behavior.
